feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 18 mai and again on 7 iunie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Teodot, Episcopul Ancirei». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 7 iunie page tells the same life — the innkeeper of Ancyra who buried the martyrs and drew the seven virgins out of the lake, taken by the governor Theotecnus — and closes by sending the reader to 18 mai for it: «Viața și pătimirea lui, împreună cu a sfintelor șapte fecioare, a fost pusă pe larg în ziua de optsprezece mai». Its «Episcopul Ancirei» is doxologia's own heading; its text has him working «sub chipul de cârciumar ... ca un episcop». Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 18 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Teodot din Ancira»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Μαΐου — «Αγίες Τεκούσα, Αλεξανδρία, Κλαυδία, Φαεινή, Ευφρασία, Ματρώνα, Ιουλία και Θεοδότη οι Παρθενομάρτυρες από την Άγκυρα της Γαλατίας και Θεόδοτος ο Μάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps her on, and it is plainly the same company: the virgin martyrs of Ancyra in Galatia, handed to the soldiers by the governor Theoteknos and drowned in the lake when they were kept pure. **The page disagrees with itself about how many they were, and that is recorded rather than resolved**: eight women are named in the calendar line and as head entries, and the verse over the narrative is headed «Εις τας επτά», for the seven, «Λίμνη γυναικών επτάς εμβεβλημένη». Nothing on the page reconciles the two counts and nothing here does either. **The eighth, Theodote, has no folder and is a new one in batch `el-05-18`.** **No year is printed for the women**, so no `dates` object is added; the Theodotus head entry on the same page carries «(; - 304)». **No hymn stands on this page**, only the synaxarion verses. **He is the ninth head name on that page and saint.gr lists him twice on this one day**: once there, «Αγιος Θεοδοτος ο Μαρτυρας (; - 304)», and again as a listing of its own at https://www.saint.gr/2260/saint.aspx, whose body says the same thing in other words — nephew of the holy martyr Thecusa, martyred at Ancyra in 304 under Maximian (285–305), who drew the women's relics out by night and buried them reverently, was seized by the tyrant Theoteknos, beheaded after many tortures, and whose own relics Theoteknos gave to the fire. **Two listings, one man, one row**: no second folder is made and the duplicate is recorded here. **The Greek supplies the year the corpus does not hold**, 304, and the emperor's reign; the existing folder carries no `dates` object and is not given one here. **It confirms the corpus's Romanian note about 7 June** with «βλέπε και 7 Ιουνίου». **It calls him neither innkeeper nor bishop**, where doxologia's page had both.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Petru, Dionisie, Paulin și al Sfântului Mucenic Teodot și al celor șapte», Glasul 4 — the one troparion the page prints for all the martyrs of the day

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contests received the crowns of incorruption from Thee our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tyrants and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ our God, save our souls.
